An adequate quantity of; enough.

examples.text: We have sufficient supplies to last the winter.
There is not sufficient access to the Internet in many small rural villages.

glosses: A quantity (of something) that is as large as is needed.

examples.text: We don't need any more; we already have sufficient.
Sufficient of us are against this idea that we should stop now.

glosses: Of a type or kind that suffices, that satisfies requirements or needs.

examples.text: This is a necessary condition but not a sufficient one.

glosses: Possessing adequate talents or accomplishments; of competent power or ability; qualified; fit.

examples.text: They felt sufficient to maintain their present prosperity and independence.
I have never yet felt adequate. I have never yet felt sufficient.

glosses: Capable of meeting obligations; responsible.

examples.text: ...to take the best ways we can, to make it known to the Duke of York; for, till Sir J. Minnes be removed, and a sufficient man brought into W. Pen's place, when he is gone, it is impossible for this Office ever to support itself.

glosses: Having enough money to meet obligations and live comfortably.

examples.text: I shall in this place only mention that qualification by wealth; the rather, being applyed to the deputies of towns and citties, where they use to say of a rich man, he is a very sufficient man : and the other sufficiencies and qualifications are mentioned on other occasions.

Some persons have been called, who have proved (it is true) that he was insufficient at that time, and could not pay more than 3 or 4,000l.; but the same witnesses give an account, that his ill circumstances were then known but to four or five persons of his acquaintance, and that by all other people, who had any knowledge of him at that time, he was looked upon to be very sufficient ; he had left off his business upon having raised an estate; he was of good reputation: he lived at Hackne in a house making a good appearance, with good furniture, and a great quantity of plate, till the last, till the time of his being put in prison, which was not till last year, that he surrendered himself in discharge of his bail.

glosses: A sufficient amount of; enough.

examples.text: We have adequate money for the journey.

examples.text: powers adequate to a great work
an adequate definition

glosses: To equalize; to make adequate.

examples.text: Let me giue yet one instance more, of a truly intellectuall obiect, exactly adequated and proportioned vnto the intellectuall appetite.

glosses: To equal.

examples.text: […] though it be an impossibilitie for any creature to adequate God in his eternitie, yet he hath ordained all his sonnes in Christ to partake of it by living with him eternally.

glosses: Done to satisfaction; adequate or sufficient.

examples.text: The criterion of mental health is not one of individual adjustment to a given social order, but a universal one, valid for all men, of giving a satisfactory answer to the problem of human existence.
The satisfactory results of the survey led to his promotion.

glosses: Causing satisfaction; agreeable or pleasant; satisfying.

examples.text: To own a bit of ground, to scratch it with a hoe, to plant seeds, and watch their renewal of life,—this is the commonest delight of the race, the most satisfactory thing a man can do.

glosses: Making atonement for a sin; expiatory.

examples.text: […] therefore the ſuffering of any other nature could not bee ſo pertinent, nor kindly ſatisfactory.

glosses: Somebody or something that meets requirements without exceeding them.

examples.text: They seem quite big on more selectivity in breeding and stiffer tests to divide the satisfactories from rejects. They say that even the term 'satisfactories' is wrong because it suggests a level just above mediocrity.

glosses: The rating given to somebody or something that meets requirements without exceeding them.

examples.text: I've been a good student — mostly distinguisheds and only a few satisfactories […]

glosses: Sufficient; all that is required, needed, or appropriate.
Used before a noun in the manner of words like some, a bit of, and so on.

examples.text: I've already had enough coffee today.

glosses: Sufficient; all that is required, needed, or appropriate.
Used after a noun.

examples.text: There is food enough for us all.
How many hired servants of my father's have bread enough and to spare!

But it wasn’t ransom enough.
His captors accepted it all,
But didn’t let go of the king.

glosses: Sufficiently.

examples.text: Those pears aren't ripe enough for the children to eat (them).
You've worked enough; rest for a bit.
We don't have long enough nails.

Of all the queer collections of humans outside of a crazy asylum, it seemed to me this sanitarium was the cup winner. […] When you're well enough off so's you don't have to fret about anything but your heft or your diseases you begin to get queer, I suppose.

The preposterous altruism too![…]Resist not evil. It is an insane immolation of self—as bad intrinsically as fakirs stabbing themselves or anchorites warping their spines in caves scarcely large enough for a fair-sized dog.

‘No,’ said Luke, grinning at her. ‘You're not dull enough! […] What about the kid's clothes? I don't suppose they were anything to write home about, but didn't you keep anything? A bootee or a bit of embroidery or anything at all?’

glosses: Fully; quite; used after adjectives to express slight augmentation of the positive degree, and sometimes equivalent to very.

examples.text: He is ready enough to accept the offer.
I know you well enough; you are Signior Antonio.

“[…] it is not fair of you to bring against mankind double weapons ! Dangerous enough you are as woman alone, without bringing to your aid those gifts of mind suited to problems which men have been accustomed to arrogate to themselves.”

glosses: Used after certain adverbs to emphasise that a quality is notable, unexpected, etc.

examples.text: Talking of Mr Smith, funnily enough, I saw him just the other day.
I left my camera on the train, but luckily enough someone handed it in to lost property.

glosses: A sufficient or adequate number, amount, etc.

examples.text: I have enough (of it) to keep me going.
Enough of you are here to begin the class.
Get some more plates. There aren’t enough yet.
Not enough is known yet about the causes of the pandemic.
I explained enough for her to understand the issue: there wasn't enough of an economic surplus.

glosses: Stop! Don't do that any more!

examples.text: I'm sick of you complaining! Enough!

glosses: An instance of being sufficient, or of doing something sufficiently.

examples.text: And she was neither beautiful nor handsome, but just at the point halfway between which a girl of twenty-three reaches who inherits good features and healthful figure, and who has learned to dance well, ride well, study enough, golf enough, and has attained the thousand other "well and enoughs" which include talking well and listening enough, and allow a woman to be liked and loved with so little consciousness that she never suspects she is particularly liked at all.
